Rich Links on the device vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate link preview engineering with storefront language. iOS frameworks and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Rich Links and LPLinkMetadata on the device — when users paste a URL, the system or your app can fetch metadata and render a rich link card with title, image, and domain using LPLinkMetadata and LPMetadataProvider. In-app link preview behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Link preview and URL unfurling engineering — code that implements LPLinkMetadata, custom link preview UI, Open Graph or oEmbed fetching, and paste-detection in compose views. Engineering inside the binary — not listing rewrite.
  • Rich Links marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app shows link preview cards, Rich Links, or paste URL rich link cards. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Rich Links.

An app that renders link preview cards and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe Rich Links and LPLinkMetadata preview cards on the store page, not whether link unfurling works inside the app binary.

Rich Links-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

If your English gallery shows an Underline Links toggle, do not upgrade zh-Hans copy to link preview card claims unless that frame shows Rich Links. App Preview captions are zh-Hans text on App Store marketing video previews. Auto-Play Video Previews is product-page video autoplay marketing.
